lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Rebuilt the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards around per-sensor error budgets, cutting mean time to detect incidents from 40 to 12 minutes.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Check that the code link leads to work you want employers to evaluate.
Replace the phone number, email, or URL if they are placeholders.
items.because: Placeholders should be replaced before applying.

items.says: Update “Expected” when your graduation status changes.
items.because: It belongs there only while June 2026 is still a future graduation date.

items.says: Use the same date and location formatting as the M.S. line.
Put the 2024–2025 internship above the 2023–2024 role.
items.because: Reverse chronology makes the most recent work easier to find.

items.says: Specify how incident detection time was measured if the figure comes from only a subset of incidents.
Clarify the load-test conditions if the two latency figures reflect different traffic or hardware.
Change “adds” to past tense.
Add the release-cycle baseline.
items.because: “Shortened … to 3 days” does not show how much it improved.

items.says: Split or narrow the fleet-migration bullet.
items.because: Migration, logging, onboarding, and on-call are separate contributions.

items.says: Make clear which change removed the nightly backlogs.
items.because: The backlog outcome is hard to attribute to all the listed contributions.

items.says: Clarify the baseline for the 68% backlog reduction.
items.because: It is unclear whether it was measured against the backlog at launch or another baseline.

items.says: State your specific contribution to the adapter and training data if others built the surrounding system.
Explain how dynamic batching reduced single-request latency.
items.because: Readers may see a contradiction unless the measurement involved concurrent traffic or another batching mechanism.

items.says: Identify the baseline for the 5% latency improvement.
Explain how training for accuracy, citations, and call count produced a latency gain.
Make your contribution more prominent than the list of methods.
The single-rollout GRPO stability claim needs an explanation of how advantages were computed.
items.because: Standard GRPO relies on relative rewards across multiple rollouts per prompt.

items.says: Say what measurable failure “stabilised” means.
Clarify whether you authored the rules, documented existing rules, or both.
Replace the broad AI-first practices claim with a specific change and observable result, or remove it.
items.because: “Accelerating delivery” and “improving outcomes” are not substantiated here.

items.says: Correct the stated 50% latency reduction to 33%.
items.because: A drop from 900 ms to 600 ms is a 33% reduction.

items.says: Check that reused sub-agent answers are included in the measured tool-call path.
Distinguish 12 percentage points from a 12% relative increase.
items.because: The stated change is from 71% to 83%.

items.says: Establish what the benchmark covers.
Confirm that all eight metrics run by default on every release, or narrow the claim.
Identify the statistic as Kendall’s tau if that is what you calculated.
Clarify what scores were correlated across the trials.
Clarify whether your role in the fixes was diagnosis only or included code contributions.
items.because: “Each was fixed upstream” leaves your contribution ambiguous.

items.says: Move Git out of “Programming.”
Resolve the GRPO bullet before presenting GRPO as a skill.
items.because: The review says to keep only methods you can explain in an interview.
